title_original: Beneath the Atlantic: Ayana V. Jackson Reimagines the Afterlives of the Middle Passage

blocks.text: Drawing on Afrofuturism, African mythology and the speculative world of Drexciya, ‘From the Deep’ transforms the ocean into a space of ancestral memory, resistance and imagined futures.

What if the Atlantic Ocean, a site of profound historical trauma, could become a space for imagining alternative Black futures? In ‘From the Deep: In the Wake of Drexciya ‘ , American artist Ayana V. Jackson reimagines the histories of the transatlantic slave trade through photography, immersive video, animation and installation. Presented at the Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, the exhibition marks its Canadian premiere after debuting at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of African Art in 2023.

Inspired by Detroit techno duo Drexciya’s imagined underwater civilisation, Jackson constructs a feminist, Pan-African world inhabited by water spirits drawn from African and Afro-Atlantic traditions. Through elaborate costumes, layered soundscapes and underwater imagery, Jackson challenges the historical representation of Black bodies, particularly women, while exploring the possibilities of mythology and speculative storytelling as forms of cultural reclamation. Moving between historical violence and imagined liberation, the exhibition considers how the legacies of the Middle Passage continue to shape diasporic identity and collective memory.

Rather than allowing the Atlantic to remain defined solely by loss, Jackson transforms its depths into a site of possibility, where ancestral histories are reconsidered, and new narratives of survival, belonging and freedom emerge.
This exhibition will be on view at the Museum of Anthropology, University of British Columbia in Vancouver , from 19 November 2026 to 29 March 2027.
